title: Add scheduler instrumentation for mixed prefill/decode workloads (apples-to-apples kernel comparisons)
creator: Sofia Ivanova
content:
## Context
Our FP8/INT8 sprint requires end-to-end comparisons that are not confounded by scheduler behavior. Right now we can see overall TTFT/TPOT/tokens/s deltas, but it’s hard to answer:
- Did we actually change prefill vs decode time, or just shift the prefill/decode mix via batching?
- Are kernel wins getting eaten by queueing / backpressure?
- Are we comparing the same “work” across runs (same number of prefills per unit time, same decode concurrency), especially when knobs/flags change?

This issue adds scheduler-level tracing + metrics to make mixed-workload comparisons reproducible and diagnosable.

## Goals
1) Add a stable set of scheduler metrics to break down time/throughput by phase (prefill vs decode) and queueing.
2) Ensure metrics are dimensioned/tagged so we can compare baselines vs FP8/INT8 canaries across model/GPU/region/kernel_mode.
3) Keep overhead low enough to run in benchmark harness + perf canary by default (sampling/aggregation as needed).
4) Provide a minimal “interpretation guide” for the benchmark sprint so folks don’t over-index on aggregate p95.

## Non-goals
- Re-architect scheduler logic (that’s ENG-19911 / follow-ups).
- Build the dashboards (ENG-7427); this ticket only provides the metrics + documentation needed.

## Proposed instrumentation (implementation notes)
### New counters/histograms
(All names below match PR-19855; see metric definitions doc for exact units.)
- scheduler.prefill.active_ms (histogram): time spent executing prefill kernels per request (server-side).
- scheduler.decode.active_ms (histogram): time spent executing decode kernels per generated token (server-side).
- scheduler.queue_depth.prefill (gauge/histogram): queue depth sampled at enqueue/dequeue (prefill queue).
- scheduler.queue_depth.decode (gauge/histogram): queue depth sampled at enqueue/dequeue (decode queue).
- scheduler.queue_wait_ms.prefill (histogram): time from enqueue->start for prefill.
- scheduler.queue_wait_ms.decode (histogram): time from enqueue->start for decode.
- scheduler.backpressure.events_total (counter): increments when backpressure triggers (by reason).
- scheduler.batch.size.prefill / scheduler.batch.size.decode (histogram): effective batch sizes at dispatch.
- scheduler.batch.window_ms (histogram): observed batching window per dispatch cycle.

### Tracepoints / structured logs (optional, sampled)
- scheduler_trace span per dispatch cycle with:
  - dispatch_type: prefill|decode|mixed
  - batch_size
  - queue_depth_at_dispatch
  - reason (timer, max_batch, max_tokens, backpressure relief)

We default to metrics-only; trace spans are enabled via a runtime flag and sampled (1–5%) for local debugging.

### Dimension/tagging requirements
We need consistent tags for perf comparisons:
- model_id (or model_family + variant)
- gpu_sku (A100/H100/L4)
- kernel_mode (baseline|fp8|int8|mixed) — wired via PR-19934
- region
- runtime_build_sha

Note: we intentionally avoid high-cardinality tags like request_id in metrics; request_id is only in sampled traces.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Metrics available in staging and benchmark clusters; validated non-zero on mixed workloads.
- [x] Can separate “active compute time” vs “queue wait time” for prefill and decode.
- [x] Batch size + queue depth visible; can correlate TTFT spikes with queueing/backpressure rather than kernel regression.
- [x] Overhead measured: <1% throughput impact on benchmark harness calibration runs (H100, top-hosted-models suite v3).
- [x] Documented in the perf metrics definition doc with units + recommended charts.

## Rollout plan
1) Land metrics behind an internal flag initially (default on in benchmark runner).
2) Enable in staging for 24h; confirm tagging + expected distributions.
3) Enable in perf canary cohorts once dashboards are in place (ENG-7427).

## Risks / mitigations
- Metric overhead: histograms can be expensive. Mitigation: use pre-aggregated buckets, avoid per-token per-request labeling; decode.active_ms uses per-token aggregation at batch boundaries rather than per token emission.
- Misinterpretation: “decode.active_ms” vs TPOT can diverge if streaming or network dominates. Mitigation: doc explicitly states these are server-side compute and queueing signals; not a replacement for end-to-end latency.
- Phase ambiguity: some models/paths fuse ops. Mitigation: define boundaries at scheduler dispatch boundaries, not kernel boundaries; if fused, it shows up as “active” time in whichever phase dispatch occurred.

## Testing
- Unit tests: scheduler emits expected metrics on a synthetic prefill+decode workload.
- Integration: run top-hosted-models-benchmark-suite-v3 mixed workload; confirm:
  - queue_wait_ms increases when batching_window_ms is increased
  - active_ms scales with seq_len and batch size
  - backpressure counter increments when queue depth exceeds configured thresholds

## Notes from implementation (PR-19855)
- We added explicit phase markers in scheduler dispatch code paths so prefill and decode get different histograms.
- Queue depth is sampled at enqueue/dequeue and at dispatch. We avoided a continuous gauge to reduce churn.
- We aligned naming with the Drive doc `fp8-int8-perf-metrics-definitions` so Grafana queries remain consistent.

## Comments / updates
### 2026-02-07 (Julian Moore)
Drafted metric list + boundaries. Key decision: treat “prefill” as first token compute for a request; treat “decode” as subsequent token generation. This matches how we reason about TTFT vs TPOT.

### 2026-02-09 (Omar El-Sayed)
Request: also expose queue wait histograms. Without queue_wait, it’s too easy to claim kernel regressions when it’s actually queueing from decode burstiness.

### 2026-02-10 (Allison Grant)
Please ensure tags include kernel_mode and gpu_sku; dashboards need model/GPU/mode slices to debug canary rollbacks quickly.

### 2026-02-12 (Rafael Mendes)
Perf canary note: we need a backpressure signal to explain TTFT spikes. If we can’t attribute, we end up rolling back too aggressively.

### 2026-02-14 (Julian Moore)
PR up: `pr-19855-scheduler-metrics-prefill-decode-split-and-queue-depth`. Ran calibration on H100 in benchmark cluster: overhead within noise (~0.4% tokens/s delta across 10 runs).

### 2026-02-17 (Sofia Ivanova)
Approved to merge once naming matches the perf-metrics definitions doc; please add a short section on how to interpret “active_ms vs queue_wait_ms” in mixed workloads.

### 2026-02-19 (Julian Moore)
Merged. Follow-up for dashboards tracked in ENG-7427. Added note to the Drive metric definitions doc and linked from sprint plan.

## Follow-ups
- ENG-7427: add Grafana panels for prefill/decode queue_wait and batch size distributions by model/GPU/mode.
- Consider adding a “scheduler.mixedness_ratio” (prefill_tokens / total_tokens over a window) if we keep seeing confusing mixed-workload comparisons during canary.
